1.1: A copy of the words of Lĕwi: the things that he decreed to his sons concerning all they were to do, and the things that would happen to them until the Day of Judgment.
1.2: He was in good health when he summoned them to him, but it had been revealed to him that he was about to die. When they all were gathered together, he said to them:

10.1: And now, my children, observe the things which I commanded you, since what I heard from my ancestors I have told to you.
10.2: See, I am free of responsibility for your impiety or for any transgression which you may commit until the consummation of the ages in leading Yisra’ĕl astray and in fomenting in it great evils against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
10.3: And you shall act torahlessly in Yisra’ĕl, with the result that Yerushalayim cannot bear the presence of your wickedness, but the curtain of the Hĕyḵal will be torn, so that it will no longer conceal your shameful behavior.
10.4: You shall be scattered as captives among the nations, where you will be a disgrace and a curse.
10.5: For the house which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall choose shall be called Yerushalayim, as the Book of Ḥanoḵ the Righteous maintains.

11.1: I was twenty-eight when I took a wife; her name was Melcha.
11.2: She conceived and gave birth to a son, and I gave him the name Gĕreshon, because we were sojourners in the land.
11.3: And I saw that, as concerns him, he would not be in the first rank.
11.4: And Qehath was born in the thirty-fifth year of my life, before sunrise.
11.5: And in a vision I saw him standing in the heights, in the midst of the congregation.
11.6: This is why I called him Qehath, that is the Ruler of Greatness and Reconciliation.
11.7: And she bore me a third son, Merari, in the fortieth year of my life, and since his mother bore him with great pain, I called him Merari; that is bitterness.
11.8: Yoḵeḇeḏ was born in Mitsrayim in the sixty-fourth year of my life, for by that time I had a great reputation in the midst of my brothers.

12.1: And Gĕreshon took a wife who bore him Lomne and Semei.
12.2: The sons of Qehath were Amram, Yitshar, Ḥeḇron, and Uzzi’ĕl.
12.3: And the sons of Merari were Maḥli and Mushi.
12.4: And in the ninety-fourth year Amram took Yoḵeḇeḏ, my daughter, as his wife, because he and my daughter had been born on the same day.
12.5: I was eight years old when I entered the land of Kena’an, and eighteen years old when I killed Sheḵem. At nineteen years I served as a kohĕn; at twenty-eight years I took a wife; and at forty-eight I entered Mitsrayim. See, my children, you are a third generation. During my one hundred eighteenth year Yosĕph died.

13.1: And now, my children, I command you: Reverence 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with your whole heart, and walk according to His Torah in integrity.
13.2: Teach your children letters also, so that they might have understanding throughout all their lives as they ceaselessly read the Torah of Elohim.
13.3: For everyone who knows the Torah of Elohim shall be honored wherever he goes, he shall not be a stranger.
13.4: He shall acquire many more friends than his parents, and many men will want to serve him and to hear the Torah from his mouth.
13.5: Therefore, my sons, do righteousness on earth in order that you might find it in shamayim.
13.6: Sow good things in your beings and you will find them in your lives. If you sow evil, you will reap every trouble and tribulation.
13.7: Acquire wisdom in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 because if a captivity occurs, if cities and territories are laid waste, if silver and gold and every possession are lost, nothing can take away the wisdom of the wise man except the blindness of impiety and the obtuseness of sin.
13.8: For if anyone preserves himself from these evil deeds, his wisdom shall be radiant, even among his opponents; it will be found to be a homeland in a foreign territory, and a friend in the midst of his enemies.
13.9: Whoever teaches good things and practices them shall be enthroned with melaḵim, as was Yosĕph, my brother.

14.1: And now, my children, I know from the writings of Ḥanoḵ that in the end-time you will act impiously against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, setting your hands to every evil deed; because of you, your brothers will be humiliated and among all the nations you shall become the occasion for scorn.
14.2: For your father, Yisra’ĕl, is pure with respect to all the impieties of the kohenim, - who shall lay their hands on the Savior. -
14.3: As the shamayim is pure above the earth, and you should be the lights of Yisra’ĕl as the sun and the moon.
14.4: For what will all the nations do if you become darkened with impiety? You will bring down a curse on our nation, because you want to destroy the light of the Torah which was granted to you for the enlightenment of every man, teaching commandments which are opposed to Elohim’s just ordinances.
14.5: You will plunder 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s offerings; from His share you steal choice parts, contemptuously eating them with whores.
14.6: And out of covetousness you will teach the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, wedded women shall you pollute, and the virgins of Yerushalayim shall you defile; and with harlots and adulteresses shall you be joined, and the daughters of the gentiles shall you take to wife, purifying them with an unlawful purification; and your union shall be like unto Seḏom and Amorah.
14.7: You will be inflated with pride over your kehunnah, exalting yourselves not merely by human standards but contrary to the commands of Elohim.
14.8: With contempt and laughter you will deride the qodesh things.

15.1: Therefore the Miqdash which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chose shall become desolate through your uncleanness, and you will be captives in all the nations.
15.2: And you shall be to them a revolting thing, and you shall receive scorn and eternal humiliation through the just judgment of Elohim.
15.3: All who hate you will rejoice at your destruction.
15.4: And unless you had received mercy through Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Ya’aqoḇ, our fathers, not a single one of your descendants would be left on the earth.

16.1: Now I have come to know that for seventy weeks you shall wander astray and profane the kehunnah and defile the sacrificial altars.
16.2: You shall set aside the Torah and nullify the words of the neḇi’im by your wicked perversity. You persecute just men: and you hate the pious; the word of the faithful you regard with revulsion.
16.3: A man who by the power of the Most High renews the Torah, you name ‘Deceiver’, and finally you shall plot to kill Him, not discerning His eminence; by your wickedness you take innocent blood on your heads.
16.4: I tell you, on account of Him your qodesh places shall be razed to the ground.
16.5: You shall have no place that is clean, but you will be as a curse and a dispersion among the nations until He will again have regard for you, and will take you back in compassion.

17.1: Because you have heard about the seventy weeks, listen also concerning the kehunnah.
17.2: In each Yoḇĕl there shall be a kehunnah: In the first Yoḇĕl the first person to be anointed to the kehunnah will be great, and he shall speak to Elohim as father; and his kehunnah shall be fully satisfactory to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and in the days of his joy, he shall rise up for the deliverance of the world.
17.3: In the second Yoḇĕl the anointed one shall be conceived in sorrow of the beloved one, and his kehunnah shall be praised and shall be esteemed by all.
17.4: The third kohĕn shall be overtaken by grief, and,
17.5: the fourth kehunnah shall be with sufferings, because injustice shall be imposed upon him in a high degree, and all Yisra’ĕl shall hate each one his neighbor.
17.6: The fifth shall be overcome by darkness;
17.7: Likewise the sixth and the seventh.
17.8: In the seventh there shall be pollution such as I am unable to declare in the presence of human beings, because only the ones who do these things understand such matters.
17.9: Therefore they shall be in captivity and will be preyed upon; both their land and their possessions shall be stolen.
17.10: And in the fifth week they shall return to the land of their desolation, and shall restore anew the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.11: In the seventh week there will come kohenim; idolaters, adulterers, money lovers, arrogant, Torahless, voluptuaries, pederasts, those who practice bestiality.

18.1: When vengeance will have come upon them from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the kehunnah will lapse.
18.2: And then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will raise up a new kohĕn to whom all the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will be revealed. He shall effect the judgment of truth over the earth for many days.
18.3: And His star shall rise in the shamayim like a Meleḵ; kindling the light of knowledge as day is illumined by the sun. And He shall be extolled by the whole inhabited world.
18.4: This One will shine forth like the sun in the earth; He shall take away all darkness from under the shamayim, and there shall be peace in all the earth.
18.5: The shamayim shall greatly rejoice in His days and the earth shall be glad; the clouds will be filled with joy and the knowledge of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will be poured out on the earth like the water of the seas. And the messengers of praise of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s presence will be made glad by Him.
18.6: The shamayim will be opened, and from the Hĕyḵal of splendor qodeshah will come upon Him, with a fatherly voice, as from Aḇraham to Yitsḥaq.
18.7: And the splendor of the Most High shall burst forth upon Him. And the Ruaḥ of understanding and qodeshah shall rest upon Him in the water.
18.8: For He shall give the Greatness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to those who are His children in truth forever. And there shall be no successor for Him from generation to generation forever.
18.9: And in His kehunnah the nations shall be multiplied in knowledge on the earth, and they shall be illumined by the favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, but Yisra’ĕl shall be diminished by her ignorance and darkened by her grief. In His kehunnah sin shall cease and Torahless men shall rest from their evil deeds, and righteous men shall find rest in Him.
18.10: And He shall open the gates of Paradise, He shall remove the sword that has threatened since Aḏam,
18.11: and He will grant to the elect to eat of the tree of life.
18.12: And Beliya’al shall be bound by Him. And He shall grant to His children the authority to trample on wicked spirits.
18.13: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will rejoice in His children; He will be well pleased by His beloved ones forever.
18.14: Then Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Ya’aqoḇ will rejoice, and I shall be glad, and all the elect shall be clothed in righteousness.

19.1: And now, my children, you have heard everything. Choose for yourselves light or darkness, the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 or the works of Beliya’al.
19.2: And his sons replied, “Before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 we will live according to His Torah.”
19.3: And their father said to them, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is my witness and his messengers are witnesses, and you are witnesses, and I am a witness concerning the word from your mouth.”
19.4: And his sons said, “We are witnesses.” Then Lĕwi finished giving instructions to his sons. He stretched out his feet on his bed and was gathered to his fathers, having lived a hundred and thirty-seven years.
19.5: And they put him in a coffin and later buried him in Ḥeḇron with Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Ya’aqoḇ.

2.1: I, Lĕwi, was born in Ḥaran and came with my father to Sheḵem.
2.2: I was a youth, about twenty years old. It was then that, together with Shim’on, I performed vengeance against Ḥamor because of our sister, Dinah.
2.3: As I was tending the flocks in Aḇĕl-Maoul a ruaḥ of understanding from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came upon me, and I observed all human beings making their way in life deceitfully. Sin was erecting walls and injustice was ensconced in towers.
2.4: I kept grieving over the race of the sons of men, and I prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that I might be delivered.
2.5: Then sleep fell upon me, and I beheld a high mountain, and I was on it.
2.6: And behold, the shamayim was opened, and a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to me: ‘Lĕwi, Lĕwi, enter!
2.7: And I entered the first shamayim, and saw there much water suspended.
2.8: And again I saw a second shamayim much brighter and more lustrous, for there was a measureless height in it.
2.9: And I said to the messenger, ‘Why are these things like this?’ And the messenger said to me, ‘Do not be amazed concerning this, for you shall see another shamayim more lustrous and beyond compare.
2.10: And when you have mounted there, you shall stand near 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. You shall be his kohĕn and you shall tell forth His mysteries to men. You shall announce the One who is about to redeem Yisra’ĕl.
2.11: Through you and Yahuḏah, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will be seen by men.
2.12: Your ḥai shall be from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s provision; He shall be to you as field and vineyard and produce, as silver and gold.

3.1: Listen, therefore, concerning the shamayim which has been shown to you.
3.2: The lowest is dark for this reason: It sees all the injustices of humankind,
3.3: and contains fire, snow, and ice, ready for the day determined by Elohim’s righteous judgment. In it are all the ruaḥoth of those dispatched to achieve the punishment of mankind.
3.4: In the uppermost shamayim of all dwells the Great Splendor in the Most Qodesh, superior to all qodeshah.
3.5: There with him are the chief messengers, who minister and make propitiation to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for all the sins of ignorance of the righteous.
3.6: They present to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 a pleasing odor, a rational and bloodless oblation.
3.7: In the shamayim below them are the messengers who carry the responses to the Messengers of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s presence.
3.8: There with him are thrones and authorities; there praises to Elohim are offered eternally.
3.9: So when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looks upon us we all tremble. Even the shamayim and earth and the abysses tremble before the presence of his majesty.
3.10: But the sons of men, being insensitive to these matters, keep sinning and provoking the anger of the Most High.

4.1: Know, then, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will affect judgment on the sons of men. For even when stones are split, when the sun is extinguished, the waters are dried up, fire is cowed down, all creation is distraught, invisible spirits are vanishing, and Gĕy-Hinnom is snatching spoils by sufferance of the Most High, men – unbelieving still – will persist in their wrongdoing. Therefore they shall be condemned with punishment.
4.2: The Most High has given heed to your prayer that you be delivered from wrongdoing, that you should become a son to Him, as minister and kohĕn in His presence.
4.3: The light of knowledge you shall light up in Ya’aqoḇ, and you, shall be as the sun for all the posterity of Yisra’ĕl.
4.4: Beraḵah shall be given to you and to all your posterity until through His Bĕn’s compassion 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall visit all the nations forever, - although your sons will lay hands on Him in order to impale Him. -
4.5: Therefore counsel and understanding have been given to you so that you might give understanding to your sons concerning this.
4.6: Because those who baraḵ Him shall be baruḵ, those who curse Him shall be destroyed.

5.1: At this moment the messenger opened for me the gates of the shamayim and I saw the Qodesh Most High sitting on the throne.
5.2: And He said to me, ‘Lĕwi, to you I have given the beraḵah of the kehunnah until I shall come and dwell in the midst of Yisra’ĕl.
5.3: Then the messenger led me back to the earth, and gave me a shield and a sword, and said to me, ‘Perform vengeance on Sheḵem for the sake of Dinah, your sister, and I shall be with you, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent me.
5.4: At that time I put an end to the sons of Ḥamor, as is written in the tablets of the fathers.
5.5: And I said to him, ‘I beg you, Aḏonai, teach me Your Name, so that I may call on You in the day of tribulation.
5.6: And he said, ‘I am the messenger who makes intercession for the nation Yisra’ĕl, that they might not be beaten.
5.7: And after this I awoke and baraḵ the Most High.

6.1: And as I was going to my father, I found a brass shield. This the name of the mountain is Aspis, which is near Geḇal to the right of Aḇima.
6.2: And I guarded these words in my heart.
6.3: Then I advised my father and Re’uḇĕn that they tell the sons of Ḥamor that they should be circumcised, because I was filled with zeal on account of the abominable thing they had done to my sister.
6.4: And I destroyed Sheḵem first, and Shim’on destroyed Ḥamor.
6.5: Then my brother came and destroyed that city by the sword.
6.6: When my father heard of this he was angry and sorrowful, because they had received circumcision and died, and so he passed us by in his bireḵoth.
6.7: This we sinned in doing this contrary to his opinion, and he became sick that very day.
6.8: But I saw that Elohim’s sentence was ‘Guilty,’ because they had wanted to do the same thing to Sarah and Riḇqah that they did to Dinah, our sister. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 prevented them.
6.9: They persecuted Aḇraham when he was a nomad, and they harassed his flocks when they were pregnant, and they grossly mistreated El’azar, who had been born in this house.
6.10: This is how they treated the nomadic people, seizing their wives and murdering them.
6.11: But the wrath of Elohim ultimately came upon them.

7.1: And I said to my father, Ya’aqoḇ, ‘Through you 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will bring the Kena’anites to nothing and will give their land to you and your descendants after you.
7.2: For from this day forward, Sheḵem shall be called City of the Senseless, because as one might scoff at a fool, so we scoffed at them,
7.3: because by defiling my sister they committed folly in Yisra’ĕl.
7.4: And we left there and came to Bĕyth Ĕl.

8.1: There I again saw the vision as formerly, after we had been there seventy days.
8.2: And I saw seven men in white clothing, who were saying to me, ‘Arise, put on the vestments of the kehunnah, the crown of righteousness, the oracle of understanding, the robe of truth, the breastplate of faith, the turban for the head, and the apron for neḇuah power,
8.3: each carried one of these and put them on me and said, ‘From now on be a kohĕn, you and all your posterity.
8.4: The first anointed me with qodesh oil and gave me a staff.
8.5: The second washed me with pure water, fed me by hand with bread and qodesh wine, and put on me a qodesh and radiant vestment.
8.6: The third put on me something made of linen, like an ĕphoḏ.
8.7: The fourth placed around me a girdle which was like purple.
8.8: The fifth gave me a branch of rich olive wood.
8.9: The sixth placed a wreath on my head.
8.10: The seventh placed the diadem of the kohĕn on me and filled my hands with incense, in order that I might serve as kohĕn for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim.
8.11: And they said to me, ‘Lĕwi, your posterity shall be divided into three offices as a sign of the honor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is coming.
8.12: The first lot shall be great; no other shall be greater than it.
8.13: The second shall be in the role of kohĕn.
8.14: But the third shall be granted a new name, because from Yahuḏah a meleḵ will arise and shall found a new kehunnah in accord with the gentile model of the people and for all nations.
8.15: His presence is beloved, as a naḇi of the Most High, a descendant of Aḇraham, our father.
8.16: To you and your posterity will be everything desired in Yisra’ĕl, and you shall eat everything attractive to behold, and your posterity will share among themselves 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄’s table.
8.17: From among them will be kohenim, judges, and scribes, and by their word the Miqdash will be controlled.
8.18: When I awoke, I understood that this was like the first dream.
8.19: And I hid this in my heart as well, and I did not report it to any human being on the earth.

9.1: And after two days Yahuḏah and I went with our father, Ya’aqoḇ, to Yitsḥaq, our grandfather.
9.2: And my father’s father baraḵ me in accord with the vision that I had seen. And he did not want to go with us to Bĕyth Ĕl.
9.3: When we came to Bĕyth Ĕl my father, Ya’aqoḇ, saw a vision concerning me that I should be in the kehunnah.
9.4: And thus we came to Ḥeḇron to settle there.
9.5: He arose early and paid tithes for all to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, through me.
9.6: And Yitsḥaq kept calling me continually to bring to my remembrance the Torah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, just as the messenger had shown me.
9.7: And he taught me the Torah of the kehunnah: sacrifices, whole burnt offerings, voluntary offerings of the first-fruits, and peace offerings.
9.8: Day by day he was informing me, occupying himself with me. And he said to me,
9.9: ‘Be on your guard against the spirit of promiscuity, for it is constantly active and through your descendants it is about to defile the Miqdash.
9.10: ‘Therefore take for yourself a wife while you are still young, a wife who is free of blame or profanation, who is not from the race of alien nations.
9.11: ‘Before you enter the Miqdash, bathe; while you are sacrificing, wash, and again when the sacrifice is concluded, wash.
9.12: ‘Present to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the twelve trees that have leaves, as Aḇraham taught me.
9.13: ‘And from every clean living animal and bird, bring a sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
9.14: ‘And of all your first-fruits and wine bring the very first as a sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim. And salt with salt every sacrificial offering.’
